findings.summary: The page close is gone, and with it the dot field, which now appears nowhere in this sample. The blog ends both its home and about pages with a real final call to action, a newsletter form. Published 1.1.0 built that block as the centered two-tone statement over the dot field, with a mono label and pills. Here it is a plain split row: a small 'Subscribe to the newsletter' title on the left and a bare form on the right. The spec caused this: the Applying row now reads 'Page close (optional)' and gives no trigger, and the new intro says 'never adds parts to match the row', so the agent took optional to mean skip it. Dropping the invented closing on the store grid was the right result for the update's goal. Dropping it where the page really ends in an action is a loss against the published version, and the closing statement is a trait of the reference too ('Built for the future. Available today.' centered with its pills at the foot of p1).
findings.promptFix: Applying the concept → Page close: replace 'optional' with a trigger. 'When a page ends in one final action for the reader (subscribe, sign up, start, contact, buy), that existing block is the page close: one centered two-tone statement over the dot field, the mono label above it, and the block's own form or pills under it. A page with no final action gets no page close; never add an action to make one.'

findings.summary: Plate captions now repeat what sits right next to them, so the figure carries no information of its own. On every store card the plate reads 'NO. 01 · BAG' about 40px above the mono meta 'BAGS · 3 COLORS', and the item detail repeats it ('NO. 01 · BAG' beside 'BAGS · 3 COLORS'). The project detail plate reads 'NO. 01 · ACTIVE' beside an Active badge, and the payment plate reads 'NO. 4242 · VISA' beside 'Visa ending in 4242'. Published 1.1.0 captioned the same cards with a real attribute from the item's own details ('FIG 01 · 18 OZ CANVAS', and that fabric is listed in the product's details), distinct from the category label under it. The spec caused this. Its examples are now `FIG 03 · ATTRIBUTE` and `NO. 07 · CATEGORY`, and 'use its type or category' is the fallback. It also says 'never the number or category alone' yet shows number plus category as an example, and it never says the caption must differ from the labels around it. So agents reach for the category even when the item has better data. The reference's thumbnails never echo their own headline (p1 changelog cards).
findings.promptFix: Signature 4 → What: 'The caption's attribute is one the item really has and that no label within the same card, row or screen head already shows. Prefer a concrete property from the item's own data (material, size, format, length, count). Use the item's type or category only when nothing else is shown. If every attribute is already visible nearby, the caption is the number and the item's kind name. Never a status, a name or a value repeated from beside the plate.' Replace the `NO. 07 · CATEGORY` example with one showing an attribute that is not on screen.

findings.summary: The plate has spread past missing item images. Billing gives the saved payment card a generative plate (bars), a decorative figure for a record that is not an item in a list or grid. This follows from the broadened 'every item without an image of its own'. The reference keeps its generated thumbnails to content cards (p1 changelog row).

Blog grid captions mix two kinds of fact in one row: 'NO. 02 · WRITING' and 'NO. 04 · PROCESS' next to 'NO. 03 · 2 MIN' and 'NO. 07 · 1 MIN'. The agent fell back to reading time when the tag would pass the 18-character cap (agent-report.md, 'Plate captions'). The spec gives the cap but no rule that captions in one list use the same kind of fact.

Dashboard overview: 'Deployment throughput' is titled above its stage while 'Recent activity' is titled inside its card. That leaves the card's top at about y 351 and the stage's top at about y 387, so the two panels start on different lines and end together. Published 1.1.0 showed this in 1 of 3 samples. The spec still covers only the stage side ('title above').

On the dashboard KPIs, '−2 since Monday' (open incidents) and '−0.6 days' (lead time) get the danger dot, because the agent mapped the trend's direction to color. Both are improvements. Published 1.1.0 showed them green.

notes: Scope: screen step, one sample per app (<app>/20261018-231142). Gates all pass (eval-1.md). Smoke tests were not run for this evaluation; the blog agent reports 9 of 9 passing. Palette consistency is 1.0 and type consistency 0.804. Compared with the published 1.1.0 runs, which were carried from 1.1.0-rc.7: S0 = showcase/runs/graphite-blueprint/1.1.0-rc.7/<app>/20261018-022713. A major counts here because there is only one sample.

Measured layout defect, commerce / repeated-drawing (desktop and mobile): false alarm. All eleven grid plates are visibly different on their crops. Kinds repeat only after all eight are used, as specKinds intends, and each repeat is a different figure: lattice d4 vs d9, wave d5 vs d10, bars d6 vs d11 (commerce/20261018-231142/drawings/home-d4..d11.png). The markup comparison strips style and class, so two figures that differ only through those attributes would compare equal.

Update goal (iterations.md, 2026-10-19, generalize): mostly reached. No invented facts in captions. No closing invented for the store grid, which ends on its grid and footer. Product detail meta now comes from real data ('BAGS · 3 COLORS'). The dashboard caps nothing artificially, and its panels end level. Mobile metric labels end in an ellipsis ('DEPLOYMENTS THIS…'). Ranked plan cards draw 1-2-3 slabs. Two side effects go too far, findings 1 and 2. Making the closing optional removed it where the product has a real final action, and the caption rule now pushes toward repeating the category.

Earlier verdicts, regressions: critic-2 and critic-4 of 1.1.0-rc.7 had no blocker or major. Held here: 48px settings-group gaps (billing and security), one left edge on the article, mobile tables with two columns and an ellipsis (team, projects, invoices), the badge word visible ('This device'), the banner directly above the actions (checkout, password, newsletter), section-current nav on detail routes, FEATURED as a mono label, no plate kind shared between the article's lead or in-body plates and its Related cards (bars and wave vs dot matrix, perspective, rings), and the about row of three at 273px, a marching pair (motion-about-m1, bp-dash 1000ms) and captions level. Nothing else is worse than published apart from findings 1 and 2.

Not raised as regressions, because the spec deliberately changed scope. Dashboard panels lost their '01 / 03' counters, and the sidebar lost its 'WORKSPACE' label: app section heads are now for multi-step flows, long forms and settings, which matches the reference's unnumbered app panels. Product Details rows lost their 01/02/03 numbers, which the update removed from the item-detail row on purpose.

Known, not re-raised (critic-2 minors). The specKinds diagonal echo in the store grid: wave at row 2 col 1 → row 3 col 2, bars at row 2 col 2 → row 3 col 3 (commerce home-desktop-light.png). The vertical pin rule beside the mobile invoice status column. Blueprint craft still uses clean single outlines rather than the reference's ribbed tiers (blog/drawings/about-d1.png vs pipeline/linear-study/reference/illustrations/p1-i5.png).

Capture artifacts, not penalized: the sticky header mid-page in blog state-newsletter-success-desktop-dark.png, state-search-empty-desktop-light.png and state-newsletter-error-mobile-light.png, and the dialog backdrop cut at y≈900 in settings state-plan-dialog-desktop-dark.png. Faint color fringes on body words in the scaled article capture look like subpixel antialiasing, not styling. Base-app content is kept: title-case post titles, 'Account Settings', the '0' cart badge. Process: the blog agent did not commit (permission), which does not affect the output.

Scores, descriptive. Reference fidelity 4: near-black and paper grounds, inverse pills, tight Inter, mono uppercase labels, split two-tone openers, hairline grids, the teal current column on a quiet stage, and the stage-lit item detail (dashboard home-desktop-dark.png, commerce products-canvas-field-tote-desktop-dark.png vs p1-desktop-light.png). Cross-app 4: one family, with the same screen heads (mono eyebrow, h1, two-tone summary), mono counts and banners. Hierarchy 4: one headline per first viewport, and the featured plate sits in the first viewport. Spacing 4: 48px groups, openers at 128px. Component states 4: an indigo ring over the red error border, an 'n fields need attention' banner, the empty dot glyph, a loading glyph on Refresh with static skeletons, the dot-meter strength, and a success blueprint with a two-tone sentence. Polish 4: only one-off items. Signature 3: stage, glyph, blueprint, plates, motion (chart-in at 420ms, marching connector) and openers are all present and built to recipe, but the dot-field closing is absent from all four apps and the plate captions lost their information (findings 1 and 2).

Verdict basis: two spec-caused majors in a one-sample screen, so the candidate does not pass. Both fixes are rewordings in the spec and do not change the design language: give the page close a trigger, and make the plate caption name an attribute that is not already shown nearby.
